text: In September 2015 we converged twice. Thirty-nine of us said "pope francis address," first spoken among us by Bernard Sanders; thirty-five said "pope francis address to" and thirty-five "address to congress," a phrase first said by Gwen Moore, peaking together on September 24. Thirty-three of us reached for "joint meeting of congress" the same day. Around September 11 a second cluster formed: twenty-nine of us said "a nuclear weapon," twenty-eight said "joint comprehensive plan of action," first said among us by Richard Blumenthal, and twenty-six said "the joint comprehensive plan of action." Twenty-five of us said "the common good," peaking again on the twenty-fourth. Two occasions, one week apart, drew us into the same words at the same time: an address to congress, and an agreement measured against a nuclear weapon. We recorded ourselves saying them, and how many of us said each.
